attempts.narrative: Four turns, four to zero, no damage taken. Nidoking's Earth Power removed Alolan Grimer on turn 1, which is the authored crack line - Power of Alchemy never had a corpse to inherit from for the rest of the fight. Alakazam's Psychic then one-shot Qwilfish and later Skrelp, and Ice Beam took Noibat at 4x through Eviolite. The only thing that went wrong on my side was a missed Focus Blast.

strategy_checks.evidence: Both player leads were at Attack -1 before the first decision point.

strategy_checks.check: Power of Alchemy copies a fainted ally's ability only while Grimer survives beside it
strategy_checks.result: PASS (negative branch, by the authored crack)
strategy_checks.evidence: Grimer was the first body removed (turn 1, Earth Power at 2x through Eviolite). No inheritance occurred at any later point, and none was claimed. The dossier's own counterplay note - 'denying the inheritance by removing Grimer first' - is exactly what happened.

strategy_checks.evidence: Turn 3 Noibat selected Tailwind, which is the authored reserve role, but a 4x Ice Beam knocked it out before the move resolved.

strategy_checks.evidence: Skrelp entered last on turn 2 and only ever selected Protect before dying; Acid Spray was never chosen, which is correct because after Noibat fell there was no faster ally to receive the drop.

strategy_checks.check: The usually faster Noibat cannot receive a retroactive same-turn boost
strategy_checks.evidence: No Acid Spray was fired, so no illegal retroactive boost could be claimed.

strategy_checks.check: Eviolite bulk supports immediate Knock Off / Poison / Water pressure
strategy_checks.evidence: Grimer selected Knock Off into Alakazam on turn 1 - the correct target and the correct 2x move - but died first. Qwilfish selected Waterfall on turn 2 and also died first. The pressure plan was chosen correctly every time; it simply never got a turn.

ai_observations: Turn 1 Qwilfish Protect was empty: it was at full HP, unthreatened, and its partner Grimer was the one being focused and the one that died. Under the September 15 no-read rule the AI cannot see my targets, so a first-turn guard is a forecast bet rather than an illegal choice, and I am recording it as an empty guard rather than a defect. It is worth noting to the AI owner that Qwilfish held Thunder Wave, which would have been a strictly better turn-1 forecast play against an unrevealed opposing pair - a speed-control move has value against every branch of the forecast, whereas Protect at full HP beside a threatened partner has value against only some.
Every other opposing choice was sensible: correct targets, correct type reads (Knock Off into the Psychic lead), and two Protects with real payoff.

level_changes.rule_applied: Won on the first attempt in four turns with zero player faints and zero damage taken. Brief rule: +1 on the weakest one or two members.
level_changes.verification: Offset-only edits, which cannot affect move legality or strategy coherence. scripts/emerald_champions_teams.py --check currently reports the generated master as stale because other authored edits from a concurrent session are also in the working tree; I deliberately did not run --write so as not to clobber that session's in-flight generation. The main agent materializes. For E0030 earlier in this block I did run --write then --check and all three gates passed.

level_changes.note: These two +1s are the rule-mandated minimum and I do not expect them to change the result. The structural issue is that this grunt fields four members against a six-member optimized party, so it is outnumbered before type matchups are considered - see the cooler note.

cooler_note: The Aqua smuggler identity is good and Alolan Grimer as the campaign's first is a real upgrade over another Mightyena. The Power of Alchemy plan is also genuinely interesting on paper. The problem is that it is a four-member team whose whole gimmick is conditional on one specific member surviving, and that member is the obvious first target for any Ground or Psychic attacker - the dossier itself names the counterplay. So the headline mechanic is, by construction, the thing a prepared player removes on turn 1. A concrete suggestion for a later pass (not applied here): either give Grimer a partner that protects it (Qwilfish already has Protect and Thunder Wave and could be authored to buy Grimer a turn), or move Grimer to the back so the inheritance has a corpse waiting for it when it arrives, which is what Power of Alchemy actually wants. Species-wise the four are well chosen for a cave-smuggler theme.

evidence.scope: Synthetic headless benchmark through scripts/playthrough/battle_driver.py against work/agent-battle-build. Not earned campaign play.
